title: Bis, Tris, & Core
notes: Happy weekend! A workout just for you, exactly when you asked for it :)

exercises.name: Dumbbell Tricep Extension
exercises.instructions: We practiced this! :D Keep your elbow facing forward without shifting it to the side. Lower the weight slowly behind your head.
exercises.description:
1. Grab a dumbbell and sit on a flat gym bench or chair.
2. Lift the weight overhead and straighten your arm.
3. Bring your shoulders back, engage your midsection, and inhale.
4. Lower the dumbbell behind your head while keeping your elbow steady.
5. Bend your arm until you feel a stretch in your tricep, and extend your elbow as you exhale.
6. Once finished, grab the weight with your other hand, and do the same number of reps.

exercises.name: Reverse Grip Tricep Pushdown
exercises.instructions: This is like the ropes but use a bar attachment and underhand (supinated) grip. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and stand tall, don't lean into it.
exercises.description:
1. Set the cable pulley to the highest position and attach a straight bar or EZ bar.
2. Grip the bar with an underhand (palms-up) grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
3. Bring your elbows to your sides and take a small step back.
4. Stand tall with your chest up and core engaged.
5. Take a breath and push the bar down until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your triceps hard at the bottom. Breathe out.
6. Slowly allow the bar to rise back up, stopping when your wrists are at roughly elbow height. Breathe in.
7. Keep your elbows locked in place throughout — only your forearms move.

exercises.name: Hammer Curls
exercises.instructions: This was my favorite exercise for a whileeee. Keep your palms facing each other the whole time, don't rotate at the top. Elbows stay glued to your sides.
exercises.description:
1. Grab a pair of dumbbells and stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Let your arms hang at your sides with your palms facing your thighs — neutral (hammer) grip.
3. Bring your shoulders back and engage your core.
4. Take a breath and curl both dumbbells up simultaneously, keeping your palms facing each other throughout.
5. Curl until your wrists are at shoulder height and your biceps are fully contracted. Exhale at the top.
6. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position as you breathe in.
7. Don't swing your torso — keep it strict.

exercises.name: Waiter Curl
exercises.instructions: Cup the top plate of one dumbbell with both hands, palms flat and facing up like you're carrying a tray or like precious mail on your mailwoman rounds. Keep tension on the biceps the whole way down, don't fully relax at the bottom.
exercises.description:
1. Hold a single dumbbell vertically with both hands, cupping the top weight plate with your palms facing up — like a waiter carrying a tray.
2. Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart, elbows tucked in close to your torso.
3. Bring your shoulders back and engage your core.
4. Take a breath and curl the dumbbell up toward your chin, keeping the dumbbell vertical and your elbows stationary. Exhale at the top.
5. Squeeze your biceps hard at the top, holding for a brief moment.
6. Slowly lower the dumbbell back down, stopping just before your arms fully extend to keep tension on the biceps. Breathe in.
7. Repeat for all reps.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.instructions: Stack your feet or stagger them for more stability. Keep your hips lifted, don't let them sag toward the floor. Squeeze your core and glutes the whole time.
exercises.description:
1. Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked on top of each other.
2. Prop yourself up on your forearm, elbow directly under your shoulder.
3. Engage your core and lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
4. Keep your top hand on your hip or extend it toward the ceiling.
5. Hold the position, breathing steadily. Don't let your hips drop or rotate.
6. After your time is up, switch sides and repeat.
